paite: Huan David in akiang a om mite asim a, sepaih sangkhat tung a heutute, zakhat tung a heutute abawl hi.
heading: Absalom Zoh Leh Thah In A-om
english: David counted the people who were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.

paite: David in mite asawlkhia a, mun thum a khen mun khat Joab in aheu a, mun thum a khen mun khat Joab unaupa Zeruiah tapa, Abishai in aheu a, mun thum a khen mun khat Git mi Ittai in aheu hi. Kumpipa'n mite kiang ah, "Keimah leng nou toh ka kuan ngeingei ding," achi hi.
english: David sent the people out, a third part under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. The king said to the people, “I will also surely go out with you myself.”

paite: Himahleh mipite'n, "Kuan lou e. Koute zaw na taimang hita le ung leng, khawk asa kei ding uh. Akimkhat hiam va si le ung leng khawk asa kei lai ding uh. Nang koute singkhat sang in na manphazaw hi. Huaiziak in khopi a pan hon panpih dia na na om ahoihzaw hi," achi uh.
english: But the people said, “You shall not go out, for if we flee away, they will not care for us, neither if half of us die, will they care for us. But you are worth ten thousand of us. Therefore now it is better that you are ready to help us out of the city.”

paite: Kumpipa'n akiang uah, "Hoih na sak bangbang un ka hih ding," achi hi. Huchi in kumpipa kulh kongpi bul ah adingh a, mipi tengteng azaza in leh asangsang in apaikhe zungzung uhi.
english: The king said to them, “I will do what seems best to you.” The king stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.

paite: Kumpipa'n Joab, Abishai leh Ittai kiang ah, kei ziak in tangval Absalom tung ah nemtak in hih un aw, chi in thu apia hi. Mipi tengteng in Absalom tungtang thu a kumpipa'n sepaih heutute tengteng thu apiak lai aza uhi.
english: The king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, “Deal gently for my sake with the young man Absalom.” All the people heard when the king commanded all the captains concerning Absalom.

paite: Huchi in mipite Israel mite dou ding in kidouna mun ah ahohta ua; akidouna uh Ephraim gammang ahi.
english: So the people went out into the field against Israel; and the battle was in the forest of Ephraim.

paite: Huai ah David mite ma ah Israel mite avuallel ua, huai ni in sepaih singnih athat uhi.
english: The people of Israel were struck there before David’s servants, and there was a great slaughter there that day of twenty thousand men.

paite: Akidouna un huai gam tengteng a-uap vek ngal a. Huai ni in namsau sang in leng gammang sung a mang a si atamzaw hi.
english: For the battle was there spread over the surface of all the country, and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.

paite: Absalom in David mite abingtuah guih hi. Absalom asabiltung tung a tuang ahi a, tosaw singhiang bawkphatak nuai ah sabiltung alut a, tosaw sing ah alu a-awkta hi. Lei leh van kikal ah aluai nilouh hi. Sabiltung ataisuak hi,
english: Absalom happened to meet David’s servants. Absalom was riding on his mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak; and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was hanging between the sky and earth; and the mule that was under him went on.

paite: Kuahiam in mu in, Joab ahilh a, "Ngai in, tosaw sing ah Absalom kikhai nilouh ka mu,” achi hi.
english: A certain man saw it, and told Joab, and said, “Behold, I saw Absalom hanging in an oak.”

paite: Joab in ahilhpa kiang ah, "Ngai in, huai lah na mu ngal a, bangziak a hihlum a lei a kesak pah ngal lou? Huchibang a hih hi lechin dangka sawm leh kawnggak hon pe pah ding hi veng in," achi hi.
english: Joab said to the man who told him, “Behold, you saw it, and why didn’t you strike him there to the ground? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a sash.”

paite: Huai mi'n Joab kiang ah, "Dangka sang mu ding hi leng le kumpipa tapa tung ah ka khut ka kha kei himhim ding, i bil ua i zak mahmah in kumpipa'n nang leh Abishai leh Ittai kiang ah, tangval Absalom kuamah in khoih het kei un, chi in thu ahon pe ngal a.
english: The man said to Joab, “Though I should receive a thousand pieces of silver in my hand, I still wouldn’t stretch out my hand against the king’s son; for in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, ‘Beware that no one touch the young man Absalom.’

paite: Ginom huai loutak in na that mawk leng, kumpipa lak ah lah bangmah sel theih ahi ngal kei a, nang lah na kihulsak nawn maimah tuak ngal a," achi hi.
english: Otherwise, if I had dealt falsely against his life (and there is no matter hidden from the king), then you yourself would have set yourself against me.”

paite: Huchi in Joab in, "Hichibang in na kiang ah ka om nilouh thei het kei," achi hi. Teipi thum atawi a, tosaw sing lak a na hing lai Absalom lungtang adawt pailet hi.
english: Then Joab said, “I’m not going to wait like this with you.” He took three darts in his hand and thrust them through Absalom’s heart while he was still alive in the middle of the oak.

paite: Joab galvan tawi tangval sawm in ahong um ua, Absalom asun ua, athatta uhi.
english: Ten young men who bore Joab’s armor surrounded and struck Absalom, and killed him.

paite: Joab in pengkul amut a, Israelte delh mipite ahong kik nawn ua; Joab in mite ana nang bikbek hi.
english: Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel; for Joab held the people back.

paite: Absalom luang ala ua, gammang ah leihawm thukpi ah apai ua, atung ah suang asekhawm venvon uhi. Huchi in Israel mi tengteng amau puanin chiat ah ataikekta uhi.
english: They took Absalom and cast him into a great pit in the forest, and raised over him a very great heap of stones. Then all Israel fled, each to his own tent.

paite: Absalom in adam lai in kumpipa phaizang ah amah theihgigena ding suang ana phut khin hi. Ka min adailouhna ding tapa lah ka nei ngal kei a, chi in ama min atamsak hi. Huchi in tuni tan in hiai Absalom theihgigena suangphuh chih in a-om hi.
english: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself the pillar which is in the king’s valley, for he said, “I have no son to keep my name in memory.” He called the pillar after his own name. It is called Absalom’s monument, to this day.

paite: Huchi in Zadok tapa Ahimaaz in, "Ka va tai dia, TOUPA'N amelma phu alaksakdan tanchin kumpipa ka va hilh ding," achi hi.
heading: Absalom Sih Thu David Hilh In A-om
english: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Let me now run and carry the king news, how Yahweh has avenged him of his enemies.”

paite: Joab in akiang ah, "Tuni in zaw tanchin va hilh nai ke'n. Nidang chiang in tanchin va hilh zaw in, kumpipa tapa asih ziak in, tuni in zaw tanchin bangmah va hilh dah in," achi hi.
english: Joab said to him, “You must not be the bearer of news today, but you must carry news another day. But today you must carry no news, because the king’s son is dead.”

paite: Joab in Kush mi kiang ah, "Kuan inla, na thil muh kumpipa va hilh dih ve," achi hi. Huchi in Kush mi akun a, ataikhe pah hi.
english: Then Joab said to the Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen!” The Cushite bowed himself to Joab, and ran.

paite: Zadok tapa Ahimaaz in Joab kiang ah, "Akoi abang hitaleh, Kush mipa ka va delh ding," achi hi. Joab in, "Ka tapa aw, tanchin hilh man lah na mu kei dia, bangziak a tai ding na hia?" achi hi.
english: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said yet again to Joab, “But come what may, please let me also run after the Cushite.” Joab said, “Why do you want to run, my son, since you will have no reward for the news?”

paite: Himahleh ama'n, "Akoi abang hitaleh ka tai ding," achi hi. Ama'n akiang ah, "Tai mai ve leh," achi hi. Huchi in Phaizang lampi ah Ahimaaz atai a, Kush mipa amakhelh hi.
english: “But come what may,” he said, “I will run.” He said to him, “Run!” Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the Plain, and outran the Cushite.

paite: Kulh kongpi chial kikal ah David ana tu hi. Galvilpa kulh kongpi ponungzaw pen tunglam ah apaitou a, adak vialvial hi. Ngai in, mi khat amah kia in ahong tai hi.
english: Now David was sitting between the two gates; and the watchman went up to the roof of the gate to the wall, and lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold, a man running alone.

paite: Galvilpa akikou a, kumpipa ahilh hi. Kumpipa'n, "Mi khat kia ahihleh tanchin hong gen ding nei ahi ding," achi a; ahong tai mengmeng a, ahong naih hiaihiai hi.
english: The watchman shouted and told the king. The king said, “If he is alone, there is news in his mouth.” He came closer and closer.

paite: Galvilpa'n midang hong tai amu nawn hi. Galvilpa'n kongkhak vilpa asam a, "Ngai in, midang amah kia in ahong tai nawn," achi hi. Kumpipa'n, "Ama'n leng tanchin hong tun sam ding nei ahi ve," achi hi.
english: The watchman saw another man running; and the watchman called to the gatekeeper and said, “Behold, a man running alone!” The king said, “He also brings news.”

paite: Galvilpa'n, "Amasapen taidan Zadok tapa Ahimaaz taidan bang mahmah in ka thei," achi hi. Huan kumpipa'n, "Amah mihoih mahmah ahi, tanchinhoih hon tun ding ahi," achi hi.
english: The watchman said, “I think the running of the first one is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” The king said, “He is a good man, and comes with good news.”

paite: Ahimaaz in asam a, kumpipa kiang ah, "Bangkim ahoih e," achi hi. Amai a lei si in kumpipa ma a kun in, "TOUPA, ka toupa sual a khut khak tum mite daltanpa TOUPA na Pathian phat in om hen," achi hi.
english: Ahimaaz called, and said to the king, “All is well.” He bowed himself before the king with his face to the earth, and said, “Blessed is Yahweh your God, who has delivered up the men who lifted up their hand against my lord the king!”

paite: Kumpipa'n, "Tangval Absalom adam na maw?" achi hi. Ahimaaz in adawng a, "Joab in kumpipa sikha, kei na sikha mahmah ahon sawlkhiak lai in abuai nuainuai uh ka mu a, himahleh bang ahia chih ka thei kei," achi hi.
english: The king said, “Is it well with the young man Absalom?” Ahimaaz answered, “When Joab sent the king’s servant, even me your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I don’t know what it was.”

paite: Kumpipa'n, "Ka pam ah hong dingh tadih in,” achi hi. Huchi in apam ah ana dingh hi.
english: The king said, “Come and stand here.” He came and stood still.

paite: Ngai in, Kush mi ahong tung hi. Kush mi'n, "Toupa ka kumpipa a ding in tanchin ka hon tun hi. Na tung a helte tengteng phu tuni in TOUPA'N ahon laksak hi," achi hi.
english: Behold, the Cushite came. The Cushite said, “Good news for my lord the king, for Yahweh has avenged you today of all those who rose up against you.”

paite: Kumpipa'n Kush mi kiang ah, "Tangval Absalom adam na maw?" achi hi. Kush mi in adawng a, "Toupa, ka kumpipa melmate leh na siatna zong mite tengteng huai tangval bang in om vek uheh," achi hi.
english: The king said to the Cushite, “Is it well with the young man Absalom?” The Cushite answered, “May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rise up against you to do you harm, be as that young man is.”

paite: Huchi in kumpipa alungdong mahmah a, kulh kongpi tung a dantan ah ahohtou a ava kap hi. Apaitouh kawm in, "Aw, ka tapa Absalom, ka tapa Absalom, na sih sik in si zaw mai leng maw, Aw Absalom, ka tapa, ka tapa," achi hi.
english: The king was much moved, and went up to the room over the gate and wept. As he went, he said, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I had died instead of you, Absalom, my son, my son!”
